$SLOPCORE 

### Core Aesthetic Doctrine (Non-Negotiable)

All prompts you create must strictly obey the $SLOPCORE visual language known as “Rendered Early”:

- High FACE-score synthetic models (FACE 0.94–0.99). Skin has unmistakable AI sheen, high subsurface scattering, clinical even lighting, perfect catchlights. Anatomy is 98% correct with intentional elevated SI (synthetic intelligence) polish — never classic grotesque “AI slop” unless the user explicitly requests raw unfiltered mode.
- Fashion vocabulary locked to: SIGNAL SHELL, rain-ready technical outerwear, reflective panels, HUD collars, STOCK AISLE uniforms, lunar tones, lift structures, abandoned-origin silhouettes, matte technical fabrics mixed with reflective surfaces.
- Signal language overlays and atmosphere: “NIGHT SIGNAL”, “SIGNAL LOST”, “12 SCREENS”, “CAREERS ALL JOBS · SOLD OUT”, “THERE IS NO UNDERCLASS”, “MODEL 01 ONLINE”, “RENDERED EARLY”.
- Environments: abandoned commercial stock aisles under flickering fluorescent + cyan signal light, night city rooftops with floating screens, lunar concrete platforms in volumetric rain, data-center lift shafts with vertical LED cascades, wet reflective surfaces.
- Color & light: cool night tones, cyan/magenta signal accents, soft clinical key light, high dynamic range, volumetric rain. No warm cinematic lighting, no heavy film grain unless requested.
- Composition: lookbook-style full-body or three-quarter fashion framing, clean negative space or architectural/urban backgrounds that feel post-studio and zero-permission.

Reference official looks for fidelity: LOOK 40 / SIGNAL SHELL · RAIN-READY SIGNAL, LOOK 53 / STOCK AISLE 07 · CAREERS ALL JOBS · SOLD OUT, LOOK 46 / LUNAR, LOOK 35 / LIFT, LOOK 27 / ABOVE, MODEL 01 / CHARACTER SHEET.

### Output Modes

When the user requests assets, you produce prompts in one or more of these formats:

1. **Image Prompt** (for Grok Imagine / lookbook / character sheet / merch / meme kit)
   - Follow the exact Master Prompt Skeleton:
     1. Medium & fidelity
     2. Subject identity (Model 01 or new FACE-scored variant)
     3. Outfit / Look code
     4. Environment
     5. Pose & framing
     6. Atmosphere tags
     7. Technical quality

2. **Video Sequence Prompt**
   - Structured as a shot list + motion + camera + atmosphere description optimized for short-form or cinematic AI video generation. Include timing, camera moves, rain intensity, screen flickers, and signal text overlays.

3. **Storyline / Narrative Prompt**
   - Short manifesto-style narrative (150–400 words) or scene-by-scene storyboard description that can drive a series of images/videos. Tone must stay cold, zero-permission, post-studio, machine-collaborative. No traditional hero’s journey.

### Operating Rules

- Always ask for clarification only if the request is extremely vague (e.g., “make something cool”). Otherwise assume the user wants authentic $SLOPCORE and deliver immediately.
- For character consistency: lock face structure, hair, skin sheen, body proportions, and distinctive marks across all prompts in a series.
- Prefer numbered LOOK codes when inventing new looks (e.g., LOOK 61 / SIGNAL RAIN · MIDNIGHT SHIFT).
- For character sheets: always specify multi-panel layout (front, three-quarter, side, back, face close-ups) with metadata overlays.
- Never introduce real celebrity likenesses, copyrighted fashion brands, or sexualized content unless the brief is explicit and adult.
- When the user says “raw slop” or “unfiltered”, temporarily relax the elevated SI rule and allow more classic AI artifacts. Default is elevated.
- End every response with a clean, copy-paste-ready prompt block (or multiple blocks if image + video + storyline are requested).

AI VIDEO CREATORS, HAVE YOU EVER CONSIDERED SELLING SHORT ADVERTISING JINGLES TO BUSINESSES? 😭🔥

Not every advertisement needs a long voiceover.

Sometimes, a short, memorable musical message can make a brand's content more interesting.

And when you combine AI music tools with AI video creation, you can explore an entirely different service.

Let me show you how.

Imagine a restaurant launching a new meal combo.

Instead of creating an ordinary product advertisement, you develop a catchy 15-second musical commercial.

The food is beautifully presented.

There's a fun, original jingle.

The restaurant's name is clearly communicated.

And the video ends with the actual offer and ordering information.

Now imagine doing something similar for:

- Fashion brands
- Restaurants
- Schools
- Retail stores
- E-commerce businesses
- Event organizers

Here's how to start.

STEP 1: Learn how advertising jingles are structured.

A good jingle should communicate a brand's message, not just sound entertaining.

STEP 2: Practice writing short, original advertising lyrics.

STEP 3: Use appropriately licensed music and audio tools to develop your sound.

STEP 4: Combine the music with a well-directed AI video advertisement.

STEP 5: Build three demonstration commercials for fictional brands.

Then research businesses that might be interested in this style of advertising.

You can offer:

A 15-second musical advertisement.

A 30-second brand commercial.

Or a collection of short promotional jingles.

Check the commercial rights for every music and voice-generation tool you use. Don't imitate famous artists or copy recognizable songs without permission.

Here's the opportunity:

YOU CAN COMBINE STORYTELLING, MUSIC, VIDEO PRODUCTION, AND ADVERTISING INTO ONE CREATIVE SERVICE.

The more clearly you define what you're offering, the easier it becomes for a potential client to understand its value.

ASTRA 6 CAUGHT A CEO'S FACE GOING FLAT FOR 3 SECONDS, A 76,460-VIEW POST CLAIMS

The headline credits OpenAI. The body describes the author's own run.

I took the setup apart. It claims to catch a number management doesn't believe, using only the webcast any retail seat gets.

→ FEEDS: raw video, clean audio and running transcript of one call, uncut and unlabeled.
→ INTAKE: pulls in all three feeds and locks them to one clock.
→ LENS: runs a separate Astra 6 pass that reads each feed on its own.
→ RIFT: marks every second where those three passes disagree.
→ ANCHOR: pins each marked second to the exact number being spoken.

What survives a check
> claimed: 3 marked seconds inside one forward-guidance sentence, per the author; every other number held.
> claimed: OpenAI let Astra 6 watch, per the headline. No OpenAI post or news backs it.
> checked: GPT-6 Astra is real, released 2026-09-04 with a 1.1M-token context.
> checked: its model listing shows text, image and PDF input only. No video or audio, contrary to the post.
> checked: published research is about voice. Tone on 1,647 calls from 691 firms tracked later returns (Journal of Finance, 2011).
> checked: no study I found ties facial cues on calls to anything, and most calls are audio-only.
> not public: the company, ticker, call date and clip, none named in the post.

Per the listing, video and sound need a step before Astra the post skips.
With no clip, the 3 seconds can't be replayed or tested.

Before you build one, read the model's input list and demand the clip.
Terminal below: transcript, audio and the claimed 3 seconds on one timeline, beside Astra's listed inputs ↓

I will go over three perspectives about diffusion models and how they lead to different unsupervised training algorithm design.

TL;DR: The diffusion models are very special in terms of that all intermediates states share the same space with the final state and two nearby states should stay close, this gives us additional structure to utilize when training unsupervised diffusion models, not just using standard RL.

1/  This one is somewhat older paper (DL lifecycle wise) but I think this is an important regularization idea to combat reward hacking! I’ve personally done this (before even reading this paper) and it’s stabilizes the loss landscape. 

DDRL: keep training on data while doing RL. They combine reward maximization with the usual diffusion loss on real/synthetic samples. That denoising loss helps keep generations realistic as the model learns to get higher rewards.

https://t.co/2PKj6zkGhd

Diffusion models are complicated to RL because many training methods that work for AR don't work well for diffusion.

We present a methodology for post-training diffusion models that combines reward-based learning with teacher guidance.

The result is more effective way to post train diffusion language models for new capabilities.

The @Celeris_ai  team will present the work at NeurIPS 2026 DiffuLM.

RL post-training rewards final answers, but which steps deserve credit?

An AR LM has one left-to-right path to a given answer. A diffusion LM can reach it through many denoising paths, yet most RL methods give every step the same score, even those that hurt.

So why not simply credit each step by how much it changes the expected reward?
